name: Duel
description: An adversary challenges one of the PCs to single combat as the rest of the party aids them from the sidelines.
impulses: sideline the rest of the party

features.name: “I Demand Satisfaction.”
features.prompt: When an adversary challenges a PC to one-on-one combat, the PC chooses whether to accept. If they reject the challenge, they must mark a Stress, and you gain a Fear. If a PC accepts an adversary’s challenge, activate a Progress Countdown (6) and a Consequence Countdown (4). If the Progress Countdown triggers first, the PC wins the Duel and gains a favor or concession from their adversary. If the Consequence Countdown triggers first, the adversary wins the Duel and claims a favor or concession from the PC. Why was this PC chosen? What do they expect to win if they prove victorious?

features.name: Relative Strength
features.description: The Difficulty of this environment equals that of the adversary who issued the challenge.
features.prompt: Who issues the challenge? What are they fighting for?

features.name: Rules of Engagement
features.description: During the Duel, the challenged PC is the only one who can make action rolls. Other PCs can only aid the challenged PC indirectly: They can Help an Ally, initiate group action rolls or Tag Team Rolls, and use any of their features that don’t directly affect the challenging adversary.
features.prompt: Where does this conflict take place? How does the environment offer the rest of the party an opportunity to aid their ally without interfering?

features.name: Dirty Tricks
features.description: Spend a Fear to have the challenging adversary or one of their allies cheat. A PC can notice their underhanded action with a successful Instinct Reaction Roll and respond in kind. What’s off -limits in this conflict? How does the adversary’s ally bend the rules without breaking them, or break the rules without getting caught? How can the PCs rebalance the scales?
